lines.say: A server died at three A-M.
By morning, your app had quietly moved to another server, and nobody woke up.
lines.show: By morning, your app had quietly moved *to another server,* and nobody woke up.

lines.say: The thing that moved it is Kubernetes. It runs copies of your app on a group of servers.
lines.show: The thing that moved it is *Kubernetes.* It runs copies of your app on [a group of servers.]

lines.say: You don't give it steps. You tell it what you want, and it keeps making that true.
lines.show: You don't give it steps. You tell it what you want, and it *keeps making that true.*

lines.say: Think of a thermostat. You set twenty-one degrees, and it keeps pulling the room back there.
lines.show: Think of a *thermostat.* You set *21°,* and it keeps pulling the room back there.

lines.say: So you say: three copies, always.
A server dies? It spins up replacement copies on the ones that are left.
lines.show: A server [dies?] It spins up replacement copies *on the ones that are left.*

lines.say: Switch on auto-scaling, and it adds copies when more users show up, then removes them once they leave.
lines.show: Switch on *auto-scaling,* and it [adds copies] when more users show up, then removes them once they leave.

lines.say: Shipping a new version? It swaps old copies for new ones a few at a time, so the app stays up through the whole update.
lines.show: Shipping a new version? It swaps old copies for new ones *a few at a time,* so the app [stays up] through the whole update.

lines.say: That's how your app recovered on its own while you slept.
lines.show: That's how your app *recovered on its own while you slept.*

lines.say: If you build with AI, follow for the system design it quietly skips.
lines.show: If you build with AI, follow for the system design it quietly [skips.]
